42875622.label: Objectives
42875622.text: To evaluate the inter-reader agreement of the Vesical Imaging Reporting and Data System (VI-RADS) quality scoring system and to assess its impact on the diagnostic performance for detecting muscle invasion.

42875622.label: Materials and methods
42875622.text: This retrospective study included 587 patients who underwent multiparametric bladder MRI before surgery. Three radiologists (two specialists and one non-genitourinary radiologist) independently assessed VI-RADS category and quality scores. Inter-reader agreement was evaluated using weighted kappa statistics. Associations between image quality, VI-RADS categorization, and tumor characteristics were analyzed using multivariable models. Diagnostic performance for muscle invasion was assessed at predefined VI-RADS thresholds and compared across quality groups and tumor size subgroups.

42875622.label: Results
42875622.text: A total of 7/587 (1.2%), 284/587 (48.4%), and 296/587 (50.4%) scans were VI-RADS quality score 0, 1, and 2, respectively. Inter-reader agreement for the final quality score was substantial (k = 0.628-0.702). Higher VI-RADS quality scores were associated with increased T2-weighted image VI-RADS scores (odds ratio [OR], 2.95; 95% confidence interval, 1.17-7.43; p = 0.021). In tumors < 3 cm, particularly for the less experienced reader, higher image quality was associated with increased positive predictive value (PPV) and accuracy at the VI-RADS ≥ 3 threshold (PPV: 51.0% vs 22.7%, p = 0.004; accuracy: 81.6% vs 71.7%, p = 0.023). No significant differences in diagnostic performance were observed across VI-RADS thresholds in tumors ≥ 3 cm.

42875622.label: Conclusion
42875622.text: The VI-RADS quality scoring system demonstrated good inter-reader agreement. Optimal image quality improved diagnostic performance in small tumors and for the less experienced reader; however, because only one less experienced reader was included, this finding requires external validation.

42875622.label: Key points
42875622.text: Question Does image quality, assessed by the VI-RADS quality score, influence diagnostic performance of VI-RADS for detecting muscle invasion in bladder cancer? Findings Higher image quality improved PPV and accuracy of VI-RADS, particularly in tumors < 3 cm and for the less experienced reader, while having limited impact in larger tumors. Clinical relevance Ensuring optimal MRI image quality enhances the reliability of VI-RADS interpretation, particularly in small tumors and non-specialized settings, and supports standardized imaging as a prerequisite for accurate bladder cancer staging.

42881022.text: Targeted alpha therapy (TAT) has moved from a largely experimental approach into clinically relevant radiopharmaceutical therapy, although evidence varies across radionuclides and products. Alpha particles combine high linear energy transfer with a tissue range of only a few cell diameters. This permits dense, localized energy deposition but creates challenges in dosimetry, radiopharmaceutical production, quality control, contamination control, patient management, waste disposal, and regulation. This review examines evidence for safe clinical implementation and distinguishes established practice from emerging concepts and institution-specific choices. Radium-223 has the strongest clinical and regulatory foundation; actinium-225, lead-212, thorium-227, astatine-211, and bismuth-213 agents are at different stages of development. Particular attention is given to alpha recoil and daughter-radionuclide redistribution, Medical Internal Radiation Dose (MIRD)-based and small-scale dosimetry, route-dependent radionuclidic impurities, good manufacturing practice, prevention of internal contamination, renal and salivary-gland toxicity, marrow risk, and jurisdiction-specific regulatory requirements. Technologies already entering specialist workflows, including quantitative imaging, Monte Carlo transport, and voxel dosimetry, are distinguished from proof-of-concept automation and more aspirational artificial-intelligence applications. Evidence supports carefully governed TAT in selected indications and trials, but routine use remains limited by radionuclide supply, product-specific dosimetry, organ toxicity, manufacturing standardization, long-term safety data, and regulatory heterogeneity.

42918472.label: Objective
42918472.text: To compare diagnostic and biopsy timeliness, malignancy yield, and cancer characteristics between the expedited and standard screening mammography recall pathways.

42918472.label: Methods
42918472.text: An expedited recall workflow implemented in Epic enabled radiologists to flag highly suspicious BI-RADS 0 findings for telephone scheduling into reserved appointments, targeting diagnostic evaluation within 1 week. We retrospectively reviewed recalls from November 1, 2024, to January 31, 2026. Primary outcomes were the time from screening to diagnostic evaluation and malignancy yield (positive predictive value 1 [PPV1] and PPV3). Secondary outcomes included diagnostic-to-biopsy and screening-to-biopsy intervals, delayed diagnostic imaging (≥30 days from screening), delayed biopsy (≥30 days from diagnostic), and malignancy characteristics. Intervals were measured in calendar days.

42918472.label: Results
42918472.text: Among 36,384 screening mammograms, 4,647 were BI-RADS 0 (recall rate, 12.8%); 57 (1.2%) were expedited. After excluding 247 standard pathway cases without follow-up, 4,400 were analyzed. Expedited patients were older (median, 64.6 versus 52.5 years; P < .001) with shorter median screening-to-diagnostic (7 versus 25 days), diagnostic-to-biopsy (14 versus 19 days), and screening-to-biopsy intervals (24 versus 45 days; all P < .001). Delayed diagnostic imaging (7.0% versus 38.2%; P < .001) and biopsy (1.8% versus 14.5%; P = .004) were less frequent. Expedited cases had a higher BI-RADS 4 or 5 rates (96.5% versus 30.1%; P < .001) and a higher malignancy yield (PPV1, 91.2% versus 5.2%; PPV3, 94.5% versus 18.2%; P < .001). Multivariable logistic regression among 278 cancers identified mass findings (odds ratio, 3.36; P < .001) and imaging size (odds ratio, 1.03/mm; P = .003) as predictors of expedited routing.

42918472.label: Discussion
42918472.text: Radiologists identified highly suspicious screening mammography findings for expedited evaluation. Expedited routing was associated with shorter diagnostic and biopsy intervals and a high malignancy yield, supporting diagnostic resource prioritization.

42919672.text: [212Pb]Pb-ADVC001 (212Pb-ADVC001) is a prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-targeted radiopharmaceutical therapy with high linear energy transfer derived predominantly from the alpha-emission of its 212Pb payload which, upon decay, delivers potent ionizing radiation directly to the tumor. TheraPb (NCT05720130) is a first-in-human dose-escalation and optimization study evaluating 212Pb-ADVC001 in metastatic androgen pathway modulation-resistant prostate cancer (mAPM-R, formerly metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer). Phase 1 results, including available long-term safety and efficacy outcomes, are presented. Methods: Participants with progressive mAPM-R previously treated with ≥1 androgen-receptor pathway inhibitor and ≥1 taxane chemotherapy (unless contraindicated/declined) were enrolled. Escalating doses of 60-200 MBq 212Pb-ADVC001 were administered at prespecified intervals every 6, 4, 2, or 1 week(s) for up to 6 doses across 7 dose-schedule cohorts (interval 3 + 3 design). The primary objective was to determine the recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D) with primary endpoints of dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs) and adverse events (AEs). Secondary endpoints included prostate-specific antigen (PSA) response, overall response rate (ORR), and radiographic progression-free survival (rPFS). Results: Twenty-two participants were enrolled, with a median follow-up of 14.1 months (IQR 8.8-17.1). No DLTs were observed and the maximum tolerated dose was not reached. The most common treatment-related AEs (TRAE) were dry mouth (18/22 participants [82%], all grade 1-2) and nausea (14/22 participants [64%], all grade 1-2); there were no grade 4-5 or serious TRAEs. The selected RP2D are 160 and 200 MBq. At these dose levels, 12/15 (80%) participants had a PSA decline of ≥50% and the median rPFS from C1D1 was 11.2 months (95% CI 2.0-not estimable) as of data cutoff. ORR was 100%, with centrally confirmed objective responses in all 5 Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumours (RECIST)-evaluable participants treated at the RP2D. Conclusion: 212Pb-ADVC001 was well tolerated up to 200 MBq, including at weekly dosing, and showed encouraging anti-tumor activity in pretreated mAPM-R. Two RP2D, 160 and 200 MBq, are under evaluation in phase 2.

42951722.label: Purpose
42951722.text: To conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis on the uptake value of fibroblast activation protein (FAP)-targeted PET (FAPI PET) across different histopathological and molecular breast cancer subtypes. As a secondary objective, to perform head-to-head comparisons with [18F]FDG PET.

42951722.label: Materials and methods
42951722.text: This systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. Major medical literature databases were systematically searched to include studies in which biopsy-proven breast cancer patients were recruited, and uptake values for malignant primary tumors and/or metastatic lesions were reported. Meta-analyses were conducted in R (R Foundation for Statistical Computing, Vienna, Austria) using the meta package.

42951722.label: Results
42951722.text: Thirty-four studies met the inclusion criteria. Pooled average SUVmax in the primary malignancy was 11.74 (95%CI:9.95-13.53) on FAPI PET. In the studies in which SUVmax values were provided for both FAPI PET and [18F]FDG PET, on average, the pooled SUVmax was 6.19 (95%CI:4.26-8.12) higher on FAPI PET compared to [18F]FDG PET. FAPI PET showed rather consistently high uptake across all analyzed breast cancer subtypes (pooled estimates ranged from 10.27 to 19.99). Notably, in studies reporting SUVmax for IDC on both FAPI PET and [18F]FDG PET, FAPI PET showed 11.33 (95%CI:8.36-14.30) higher pooled uptake. Similarly, in studies providing SUVmax for luminal A breast cancer, FAPI PET showed 7.85 (95%CI:5.45-10.25) higher uptake compared to [18F]FDG PET.

42951722.label: Conclusion
42951722.text: Our findings suggest that FAPI PET exhibits consistently high semi-quantitative values across breast cancer subtypes and can potentially enhance lesion conspicuity and detection rate, particularly in low-[18F]FDG-avid malignancies.

42994072.label: Objectives
42994072.text: To evaluate the diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI)-derived quantitative index (μDiff) and T1 mapping-derived extracellular volume (ECV) fraction for distinguishing mild acute pancreatitis (AP) from the combined moderately severe or severe category, and to compare their discrimination with magnetic resonance severity index (MRSI) and clinical scores.

42994072.label: Materials and methods
42994072.text: This retrospective study enrolled patients with AP who underwent abdominal MRI early after admission between 2024 and 2025. MRI protocols included conventional imaging, DWI, and pre- and postcontrast T1 mapping. The DWI-derived μDiff index was calculated from signal intensities at b values of 200 and 1500 s/mm2, whereas ECV was derived from pancreatic and blood-pool T1 values. AP severity was classified according to the 2012 revised Atlanta classification. Five single-predictor and four two-predictor logistic models were evaluated using AUCs with 95% confidence intervals, paired DeLong comparisons, and 2,000-resample bootstrap internal validation; calibration and exploratory decision-curve analyses were also performed.

42994072.label: Results
42994072.text: Among 140 patients with AP, 99 had mild AP and 41 had moderately severe or severe AP. Both μDiff and ECV increased with severity. μDiff showed an AUC of 0.896 (95% CI, 0.836-0.956), with no statistically significant difference from MRSI (0.878; 95% CI, 0.811-0.946; DeLong p = 0.720). The μDiff + MRSI model achieved an apparent AUC of 0.972 (95% CI, 0.948-0.996) and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.969, with improved discrimination over μDiff and MRSI alone (Holm-adjusted p = 0.019 and p = 0.003, respectively). Its corrected calibration slope and Brier score were 0.911 and 0.067.

42994072.label: Conclusions
42994072.text: The DWI-derived μDiff index showed good discrimination of Atlanta-defined AP severity, with performance statistically comparable to MRSI. Their combination improved discrimination and retained high performance after internal validation, supporting their complementary value for severity classification.

43012972.label: Background
43012972.text: Ki-67 is a key immunohistochemical marker of tumor proliferative activity in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC); however, non-invasive assessment of Ki-67 status before surgery remains an unmet clinical need. This study aimed to develop and internally validate multi-sequence magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) radiomics models based exclusively on non-contrast sequences for preoperative prediction of Ki-67 expression.

43012972.label: Methods
43012972.text: This retrospective study included 91 patients with 97 pathologically confirmed HCC lesions ( high Ki-67, ≥ 10%, n = 55; low Ki-67, < 10%, n = 42). Three-dimensional volumes of interest were manually segmented on T2-weighted imaging ( T2WI), diffusion-weighted imaging ( DWI), and apparent diffusion coefficient ( ADC) maps, and 5055 radiomic features ( approximately 1684 per sequence) were extracted were extracted from the three sequences. After feature selection with Pearson correlation coefficient filtering and the Kruskal-Wallis test, three multilayer perceptron ( MLP) models were constructed: Model-T ( T2WI), Model-D ( DWI + ADC), and Model-M ( combined T2WI, DWI, and ADC). The models were developed with five-fold cross-validation in the training cohort and were evaluated in a held-out testing cohort. This was a single-center retrospective study, and validation was internal only. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve ( AUC), sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy.

43012972.label: Results
43012972.text: No significant differences in clinical characteristics were observed between the high and low Ki-67 groups. In the training cohort, the apparent (resubstitution) AUCs of Model-T, Model-D, and Model-M were 0.715, 0.823, and 0.860, respectively (representing model fit rather than cross-validated performance). In the held-out testing cohort, the corresponding AUCs were 0.707, 0.692, and 0.716. In the testing cohort, Model-M achieved a sensitivity of 68.8%, a specificity of 53.8%, and an accuracy of 62.1%, whereas Model-D showed the most balanced performance (sensitivity, 68.8%; specificity, 76.9%; accuracy, 72.4%). The dominant features were texture features derived predominantly from the ADC sequence. The cross-validated training AUCs were considerably lower (range, 0.522-0.585).

43012972.label: Conclusions
43012972.text: In this single-center, internally validated study, non-contrast multi-sequence MRI radiomics models integrating T2WI, DWI, and ADC showed moderate discrimination of Ki-67 expression in HCC. The contrast-free strategy is potentially applicable to patients with contraindications to gadolinium and warrants external validation; These findings represent internal validation only and require confirmation in external, preferably prospective multicenter, cohorts before any clinical application can be considered.

43019572.text: Palisaded neutrophilic and granulomatous dermatitis (PNGD) is a rare benign dermatosis typically associated with connective tissue diseases. Its occurrence as a paraneoplastic or reactive phenomenon in hematologic malignancies, particularly acute myeloid leukemia, is exceedingly rare. We present the case of a 65-year-old woman with acute myeloid leukemia who exhibited widespread, intensely hypermetabolic subcutaneous nodules on 18F-FDG PET/CT, strongly mimicking leukemia cutis. Histopathologic examination confirmed PNGD, averting a false-positive interpretation. This case highlights PNGD as a critical diagnostic pitfall in oncologic PET/CT imaging, emphasizing the necessity of histopathologic correlation for hypermetabolic cutaneous lesions to prevent inaccurate upstaging.

43056272.text: Yttrium 90 transarterial radioembolization has evolved from a palliative lobar therapy for advanced liver malignancies into a versatile potentially curative treatment across hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) stages, intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA), and liver metastases. Central to this evolution is the shift from empirical population-based activity prescriptions to personalized dosimetry, tailoring administered activity to each patient's anatomy, tumor biology, treatment intent, and microsphere distribution to optimize tumor absorbed dose while constraining normal tissue exposure. Prospective studies have demonstrated that personalized dosimetry significantly improves tumor response and overall survival compared with conventional dosing. Despite this evidence, clinical adoption remains inconsistent. In this review, the authors aim to address that gap by providing a practical intent-based framework for implementation. They present dosimetric principles, activity prescription methods, and dose-response evidence across HCC, iCCA, and liver metastases, with practical recommendations organized by treatment intent. Treatment intent, whether curative or palliative, is the primary determinant of dosimetric strategy, guiding selection of the dosimetry model, target dose, and normal liver dose constraints. The authors review pretreatment planning work flows and posttreatment verification and present a practical decision algorithm integrating clinical intent, imaging, and dosimetry modeling.

43076672.text: History A 31-year-old female patient with past medical history of uterine leiomyomas, hypertension, and migraines underwent CT for evaluation of an abdominal wall hernia, and lesions were incidentally discovered (Fig 1). The patient did not report any symptoms other than the bulge due to the hernia. Abdominal examination was negative for tenderness and palpable mass. Past surgical history included multiple myomectomies, cesarean section, and hysterectomy with bilateral salpingectomy. Laboratory results, including liver function tests, complete blood count, α-fetoprotein, carcinoembryonic antigen, and carbohydrate antigen 19-9, were within normal limits. The patient underwent MRI for further characterization (Figs 2-5).
